encounters.title: The Overturned Postal Van
encounters.description: An overturned postal van rusts on the ring road. The driver is mummified against the steering wheel. The rear doors are sheared open: scattered mail, three canvas supply packs, and one heavy, sealed manila envelope addressed to someone at the nearest settlement.

choices.text: Read the scattered letters.
Take the sealed envelope. Deliver it to the settlement.
Take the canvas supply packs. Leave the mail.
Burn the van. Clear the road hazard.

encounters.title: The Still Weather Station
encounters.description: A pre-war telemetry tower stands on a low hill, powered by a cracked solar array. The data logger is still running. A tarp is stretched under the panel—someone sheltered here recently. A clean tin cup sits upside down on a rock.

choices.text: Spool the telemetry data to tape.
Strip the solar panel off the mast.
Strip the station for copper wire and circuit boards.
Leave the station running. Take only the tin cup.

encounters.title: The Pianist
encounters.description: An old man plays a warped upright piano in the ruins of a roofless concert hall. The piano has three working keys. He plays the same three-note phrase, over and over, waiting for the fourth. He doesn't look up when you enter.

choices.text: Sit and listen. Wait for the fourth note.
Leave a portion of your rations on the piano bench.
Tell him the coordinates to your shelter.
Destroy the piano with an axe. Force him to move.

encounters.title: The Roadside Trader
encounters.description: A woman has pulled a wooden cart onto the highway shoulder. She has salt, two rusted tins of beans, and a working flashlight. She asks for medical supplies. She does not offer her name, and counts the barter goods entirely by touch. She is totally blind.

choices.text: Trade medical supplies for the salt and tins.
Trade only for the flashlight. Keep your medical supplies.
Trade everything she asks for everything she has.
Refuse the trade. Leave her on the roadside.

encounters.title: The Water Seller
encounters.description: At a highway crossroads, a man is selling filtered water by the tin cup. The filter is real—charcoal and sand packed in PVC. His price is information: he wants the coordinates of any occupied settlements. He trades water for names.

choices.text: Give him the coordinates of the settlements you know.
Take a cup of water. Give him nothing.
Demand the PVC filter, not the water.
Walk away. Selling out settlements for water is a bad trade.

encounters.title: The False Broadcast
encounters.description: A field radio sits on a cracked concrete counter, looping a broadcast: 'Come to the old school. We have food and medicine. We are many.' The transmission is crystal clear. Too clear. You monitored this exact frequency yesterday, and it was dead air.

choices.text: Go to the school to verify the broadcast.
Rebroadcast a warning on the same frequency that it's a trap.
Smash the radio so no one else hears the loop.
Ignore it. It's not your frequency to police.

encounters.title: The Two Camps
encounters.description: Two camps are pitched across a valley, both flying the same bleached white flag. One camp has cooking smoke. The other does not. A scout on the ridge says the smoking camp is a raider ambush; a scout from the smoking camp told you yesterday the ridge camp is a cannibal den. They can't both be telling the truth. But they could both be lying.

choices.text: Trust the ridge scout. Approach the cold camp.
Trust the cooking smoke. Approach the valley camp.
Avoid both. Detour three miles around the valley.
Hold position. Watch them for a full day before deciding.

encounters.title: The Sick Child
encounters.description: A child sits in a blown-out doorway, alone. Their cough is a wet, rattling heave. There are no adults visible. The child is fever-delirious; they only point to the dark house behind them and repeat a single name.

choices.text: Wrap the child in a blanket. Carry them to your clinic.
Draw your weapon. Search the dark house for the adult.
Leave water and a fever reducer on the step. Keep moving.
Leave. You cannot afford the caloric drain of a sick dependent.

encounters.title: The Pinned Scavenger
encounters.description: A man lies in the rubble of a collapsed hardware store, his leg crushed beneath a steel I-beam. He is conscious and bleeding slowly. He has a full canvas pack. He promises you half the pack if you lever the beam off him. He says you can take the whole pack and leave him the water if you don't.

choices.text: Rig a fulcrum. Free him and split the pack.
Free him, but take the entire pack as payment.
Take the pack. Leave him the water. Walk away.
Free him. Leave him his pack. He needs it more.

encounters.title: The Roof Access
encounters.description: A fire stairwell leading to a roof. The door is propped with a brick. From above, you hear the faint, high-pitched ping of a surviving radio beacon. The concrete stairs are severely degraded; the rebar is exposed, and the fourth step is gone entirely.

choices.text: Risk the climb. Vault the missing step.
Call up the stairwell. Listen for an answer.
Spend an hour shoring the gap with timber before climbing.
Leave. The beacon isn't worth a broken leg.

encounters.title: The Cold Storage
encounters.description: An industrial freezer warehouse. The main sliding door is secured with a heavy chain. The links of the chain are bright, fresh steel, recently cut and re-padlocked. From inside, the low, vibrating hum of a working compressor can be heard. Whatever is inside is being kept frozen on purpose.

choices.text: Cut the new chain with bolt cutters and enter.
Pound on the metal door. Wait for a response.
Leave a barter list pinned to the door.
Walk away. A running compressor means someone is defending this space.

encounters.title: The Hot Sign
encounters.description: A metal hazard sign beside the highway, the radiation trefoil faded to pale pink. Your dosimeter begins ticking wildly as you pass—the sign itself is highly irradiated. Tucked beneath the sign in the center of the hotspot is a locked steel ammunition box.

choices.text: Sprint into the hotspot, grab the box, and retreat.
Mark the anomaly on your map and leave.
Wait for the wind to shift the radioactive dust before approaching.
Hook the box with a long branch to drag it out of the zone.

encounters.title: The Clean Well
encounters.description: A hand-pump well in a deserted courtyard. The water runs clear. A logbook sits nearby, showing six months of daily radiation checks, all passing. The final entry, written three days ago in a frantic hand, reads: 'ONLY FOR THE LIVING.'

choices.text: Drink the water. You need the hydration.
Use a chemical reagent kit to test the water yourself.
Fill your canteens but do not drink until you return to base.
Empty the pump and leave. Do not risk it.

encounters.title: The Whiteout Traveler
encounters.description: A figure emerges through a driving snow squall, walking in the opposite direction. They are wearing a light pre-war jacket, completely unsuited for the freeze. They ask for directions to a town that was vaporized two years ago. Their voice is perfectly calm.

choices.text: Tell them the truth about the town. Offer them an emergency blanket.
Say nothing. Step aside and let them walk into the squall.
Give them directions to the nearest surviving settlement.
Grab their arm. Force them into the lee of a ruined truck.

encounters.title: The Flooded Road
encounters.description: A burst water main has flooded the low ground ahead with freezing, fast-moving brown water. A scavenged sedan is stalled in the current, water rising past the door handles. A man is on the roof screaming. A child is trapped inside.

choices.text: Wade into the freezing current. Haul the child out the window.
Throw a line from the bank. Do not enter the water.
Run for help. You don't have the body weight to survive the current.
Watch. You are on foot and the water is too fast.

encounters.title: The Silent Dogs
encounters.description: You approach a fenced farmstead. Four emaciated dogs stand in the yard. They do not bark. They are not asleep—they are watching you, ears forward, tails rigid. A dog that barks is a warning. A dog that doesn't bark has been commanded to stay silent. Someone is watching from the house.

choices.text: Back away slowly. Do not turn your back. Do not run.
Announce yourself to the house with open, empty hands.
Leave a tin of food at the gate. Withdraw.
Cut through the yard anyway. The dogs might be wild.

encounters.title: The Following Footsteps
encounters.description: On a long stretch of highway, you hear a second set of footsteps matching your pace. You stop; they stop. You walk; they walk. They have shadowed you for a mile. The crunch of boots on asphalt is too loud to be an animal, and too rhythmic to be a stumbling infected.

choices.text: Stop dead. Draw your weapon. Wait for them to appear.
Call out. Offer to share the road in the open.
Drop to a crouch and scan your back trail with optics.
Increase your pace to a jog. See if they match it.

encounters.title: The Border Camp
encounters.description: A territorial checkpoint blocks the road. It is unmanned, but a steel drum fire is still smoking. The boom gate is raised. A clipboard logbook sits on a stool, recording the last three travelers. The final entry is twenty minutes ago. The guards left in a profound hurry.

choices.text: Move through the open checkpoint at a sprint.
Sign the logbook, leave your designation, and pass.
Wait by the fire for the guards to return.
Steal the logbook. The intelligence is worth the risk.

encounters.title: The Two Factions
encounters.description: A tense parley between two hostile groups. They have summoned you as a neutral arbiter. The barter goods—ammunition and antibiotics—sit on a wool blanket between them. Neither side will touch the blanket first. They expect you to handle the goods, making you the physical guarantor of the exchange.

choices.text: Act only as a witness. Do not touch the blanket.
Touch the blanket. Assume the risk of guaranteeing the trade.
Refuse the role. Walk away and let them sort it out.
Propose a blind drop exchange instead. No blanket required.

encounters.title: The Locked Room
encounters.description: An interior security door, locked from the outside. The brass key is still in the cylinder. From inside, you hear the slow drip of water and the loud, rhythmic ticking of a mechanical clock. The lock cylinder is heavily oiled. Someone locked this room and left the key for the next person.

choices.text: Turn the key and open the door.
Pound on the steel door. Listen for breathing.
Leave the door and the key untouched.
Pull the key from the lock and take it with you.

encounters.title: The Two Graves
encounters.description: Two fresh graves dug side-by-side in the permafrost. The wooden markers bear the exact same first name, the exact same date of death, but different surnames. A clean shovel leans against a dead birch tree. The digger is gone.

choices.text: Exhume one of the graves to see what's inside.
Leave a handful of dried moss on each mound. Walk away.
Take cover in the treeline. Wait for the digger to return.
Mark the coordinates and leave the dead in peace.

encounters.title: The Beggars at the Gate
encounters.description: Three people stand at the outer perimeter fence. They are not injured or irradiated, merely starving. You have enough calories in the stockpile to maintain your crew's basal metabolic rate, calculated to the gram. The perimeter guard has his rifle lowered, looking to you for the call.

choices.text: Authorize the release of three day-rations from the stockpile.
Order them away. The caloric math cannot be broken.
Offer them the calories only in exchange for manual labor.
Give them coordinates to a larger settlement. Give them no food.

encounters.title: The Thief Child
encounters.description: A child is caught stealing from your transit packs. They have already eaten a handful of dried fruit. The child is rail-thin and crying. They belong to no known shelter. Your guard has a tight grip on the child's arm, waiting for orders.

choices.text: Give the child a full ration and release them.
Interrogate the child to find their camp.
Punish the theft. The supplies are absolute.
Take the child into the shelter as a dependent.

encounters.title: The Library Cache
encounters.description: A public library, stripped to the studs. But behind a row of ruined encyclopedias, you find a survivor cache: iodine, a thermal blanket, and a ledger. The ledger is a log of travelers who have sheltered here, taking what they need and leaving what they can. The last entry is a week old.

choices.text: Take the iodine, leave surplus ammunition, and sign the ledger.
Take only the iodine. Sign the ledger.
Leave medical supplies in the cache. Take nothing.
Strip the cache entirely. Leave the ledger blank.

encounters.title: The Greenhouse Keeper
encounters.description: A shattered municipal greenhouse. In one corner, thick plastic sheeting creates a warm microclimate. A woman is tending a single row of pale green seedlings. She leans on a double-barreled shotgun. She offers seedlings for mineral salt.

choices.text: Trade mineral salt for the seedlings.
Offer manual labor repairing the plastic in exchange for the seedlings.
Raise your weapon. Demand the seedlings.
Leave without trading. Note the location for the shelter log.

encounters.title: The Dead Radio Operator
encounters.description: A relay station. The operator is dead at the console, headphones still over their ears. The equipment is still drawing power. The logbook shows an entry from six hours ago. An automated distress loop is still broadcasting into the dead air.

choices.text: Cut the power to the broadcast. Bury the operator.
Leave the automated distress loop running. It might draw a rescue.
Strip the operator of the headphones and take the logbook.
Override the loop. Broadcast your shelter's coordinates before leaving.

encounters.title: The Ice Fishermen
encounters.description: Two figures are ice fishing in the center of a frozen lake. Three frozen fish lie on the ice beside them. They wave enthusiastically. They are standing on black ice, over the deep channel, while the white, solid ice hugs the shore. They don't seem to realize the ice under them is cracking with every step.

choices.text: Walk onto the black ice and drag them back to the white.
Yell from the treeline. Warn them about the deep channel.
Wait for them to finish. Barter for the fish when they reach shore.
Watch. If they go through the black ice, you get their gear.

encounters.title: The Quarantine Sign
encounters.description: A suburban house with a red QUARANTINE cross painted on a bedsheet hanging in the window. The paint is flaking and old. From inside, you hear a child singing a pre-war television jingle. The door is standing slightly open, unlatched.

choices.text: Kick the door wide and clear the house.
Stand back and call through the doorway. Do not cross the threshold.
Leave a half-ration on the porch and walk away.
Note the location as a biohazard. Avoid the house entirely.

encounters.title: The Last Train
encounters.description: A commuter train is idling on an elevated track, its doors open to the wind. The cabin is empty. The digital destination board is still lit, displaying a town that has been a radioactive crater for three years. The engine hums, but the tracks ahead are sheared entirely off the bridge.

choices.text: Sweep the passenger cars for abandoned luggage.
Strip the heavy-duty battery array from the locomotive.
Leave a warning in the cabin that the bridge is out.
Take cover and observe. A running train draws scavengers.
